title: Murmuration — Context Compression & Practical Notes
content:
Quick TL;DR:
- Idea: treat large conversation/history as a compressible structure (not just token-level lossy compression). Think "murmuration": local interactions -> emergent compact representation for downstream conditioning.
- Practical goal: reduce effective KV-store size by ~4x while preserving next-token fidelity on user-critical prompts (dialog QA, code patches).

Motivation / Context:
- Running into production limits on KV cache size for long-session users on Dedicated clusters. Batching helps but memory pressure (esp on A100S/Max-N) is still a bottleneck when many long sessions are active.
- Prior art skim: retrieval compression, chunking, latent-vector pooling, attention-pruning papers. Want something operational: deterministic-ish, incremental, cheap to compute on CPU, easy to store in S3/Redis, reversible-ish for debugging.

Papers & quick takeaways (read + marginal notes):
1) "Sticky Representations for Long Contexts" (ICLR 2029 workshop) — nice framing; they use iterative pooling across windows and keep per-window residuals. Good for reducing token count by 3x with small quality hit. Implementation note: their pooling pass is O(n) per-window and can be batched.
2) "Latent Chunking with Attention Heads" (NeurIPS 2028) — shows head-level sparsity aligns with topically coherent spans. Suggests we can compress by identifying head activations rather than raw tokens. Hard in practice unless we run a probe.
3) "Lossy KV Quantization for Cache Eviction" (arXiv 2029) — quant + entropy coding on KV pairs; impressive for embeddings-like kvs but less on raw token caches because of positional sensitivity.

My synthesis: combine lightweight pooling (stickiness) + occasional "anchor tokens" per span + a small residual prefix kept exact. So each span -> compressed object = {anchor-idx, pooled-vector, small-residual-subsequence}. Keep total size controlled and allow partial expansion on hot requests.

Operational constraints we care about:
- CPU-only pass doable in <10ms per 1k tokens for live-serving compression (target Dedicated use).
- Storage schema: Redis hash per-session, key order preserved, small blobs (<1KB each) to avoid Redis LRU churn.
- Fallback: full expansion on canary route or when exact match required (e.g., legal/regulatory contexts).

Mini experiment plan (priority order):
A) Offline sim: take 5k anonymized sessions (prod-ish) and try 3 compression schemes: avg-pool-by-window, sticky-iterative, and head-probe bucketing. Measure perplexity delta on next-token prediction and downstream metric (QA F1 on convo).
- Datasets: sample from Dedicated clusters (ask SRE for session dump). Mask PII.
- Metrics: token-level ppl delta, retrieval-based answer F1, patch generation diff (ROUGE).
- Timeline: 2 weeks to get baseline sims running.

B) Microbenchmark: implement CPU pooling kernel in C++/AVX (or sim with numpy first) to measure throughput. Target: 1k tokens -> 6–8ms on c5d.large equivalent. If too slow, fallback to optimized Rust.

C) Canary: integrate into staging routing with heuristic: compress >8k tokens sessions, and on first compress event, log expansion quality for 3 subsequent requests.

Open questions / risks:
- Does compression systematically hurt coherence for code editing flows? Code tends not to be compressible by semantic pooling. Need separate path: preserve code blocks verbatim.
- Latency cost on cold expand: if we expand compressed spans on a hot path, we might blow tail latency SLO. Must make expansion async when safe.
- Debuggability: operators will need tools to map compressed blobs back to readable tokens. Consider storing summary text (first N chars) alongside vector.

Notes from convo with Evan (2029-03-10):
- Evan: try per-session "heat map" where we only keep exact tokens for ~10 most-recent/high-attention spans. Rest compressed. He likes anchor/residual model.
- Kaiya: worried about metric drift if we tune compression on synthetic evals only. Need a small human eval or automated adversarial prompts.

Short list of implementation TODOs:
- [ ] Dataset export request (SRE): INF-DEPOT session dump (JIRA INF-3791).
- [ ] Prototype pooling kernel (numpy) — Lina.
- [ ] Bench harness for ppl/QA F1 — Evan.
- [ ] Storage sketch (Redis schema) + eviction policy doc — Kaiya.
- [ ] Add rule to preserve code fences and quoted texts verbatim.

Ad-hoc heuristics I'm testing in sim (notes):
- Window size 128 tokens, pool by sliding-average + L2-normalize vectors -> store 1 pooled vec per window + either first-8-tokens residual or last-8-tokens residual (empirically last works better for chat).
- Anchor selection: choose token with highest attention-sum within window (approx via LM probe). Cheap heuristic: prefer punctuation and newlines.
- Expansion strategy: lazy expand only when decode attention hits anchor or residual-high-sim threshold.

Small checklist for a README/PR when we ship prototype:
- Motivation + simple diagrams (murmuration analogy + lifecycle).
- Offline sim results + graphs (ppl vs compression ratio).
- Microbench numbers (CPU/throughput/latency).
- Storage API + fallback policies.
- Safety: PII detection + uncompressed override for flagged sessions.

Useful links & refs (quick):
- Sticky reps proto on Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Murmuration-Proto
- Git: https://github.com/redwood-inference/murmuration-proto/pull/142 (prototype WIP)
- Sketch: figma link (private) — left note in slack thread #murmuration.

Brain dump (short, messy):
- If we can compress cold-history heavily and keep a thin, high-fidelity recent window, we buy a lot for Dedicated memory.
- Need to avoid knee-jerk quantization on KV pairs; vector pooling + re-embedding might be gentler.
- Consider hybrid: first-tier = pooling, second-tier = low-bit quant on pooled vectors, third-tier = cold-archival compressed files (S3) with decompress-on-demand.

Questions to bring up in next sync with Mike/Product + SRE:
1) How many active long sessions are we targeting for Dedicated SLO? (capacity planning input).
2) Are there regulatory customers that require full verbatim retention? (affects eviction/compression rules).
3) What's the max acceptable cold-expand latency for customer-visible RPCs?

End notes / personal next steps:
- Run the offline sim (this week).
- If sim shows <1.5% ppl increase at 4x compression, okay to move to microbench.
- Keep logs for a sample of 100 sessions to sanity-check hallucination/regression.

Random thought: the word "murmuration" helps sell the idea — visualize local interactions producing a compact global pattern. But keep docs pragmatic: diagrams + simple numbers will win the PM.

-- Lina
